description: Phase 1 reusable reasoning skills for the TRACE-Net middle-ground Engram + mature LLM architecture.

skill_cards.title: Partial identifier discovery
skill_cards.description: Narrow incomplete part-number prefixes or contains clues without falsely identifying a final part.
applies_when: The user knows only the beginning of a part or item number.
The user remembers digits or characters contained somewhere in the identifier.
The user explicitly says the identifier is incomplete or uncertain.
does_not_apply_when: A complete exact identifier is supplied with no uncertainty.
The request is only about a known page, figure, or procedure.
skill_cards.reasoning_goal: Use exact partial-identifier retrieval first, deduplicate and rank candidates, explain why each top candidate matches, and ask only questions that meaningfully separate the remaining candidates.
required_first_searches: Search exact identifier indexes for the supplied prefix or contains fragment.
Search source-resolved IPL/table identifier fields before broad semantic retrieval.
Deduplicate candidate identities across graph, table, OCR, and visual guidance.
forbidden_tunnels: Unbounded semantic-only search as the first search.
Treating the first returned candidate as confirmed identity.
Using Engram examples as current source evidence.
ranking_policy: Exact prefix or contains match outranks semantic similarity.
Source-resolved nomenclature and manual/ATA agreement outrank guidance-only matches.
Candidates matching additional user constraints outrank candidates matching only the fragment.
Keep the candidate set diverse and do not repeat aliases as separate candidates.

evidence_sufficiency.direct_answer_requires: A source-resolved exact identity that satisfies the supplied fragment and current constraints.
evidence_sufficiency.candidate_mode_when: One or more credible matches exist but the supplied clue does not uniquely identify a part.
evidence_sufficiency.guidance_mode_when: Only visual, semantic, OCR, graph, or summary leads exist without source resolution.

answer_mode_rules.direct_if: A unique source-resolved candidate exists and the current evidence permits the exact claim.
answer_mode_rules.fail_closed_if: No source-resolved or credible candidate evidence exists after bounded retrieval.

answer_requirements: Lead with the number of useful candidates or the strongest current candidate.
For each displayed candidate, explain which part of the user clue it matches.
State what prevents final identification without repeating generic disclaimer sections.
Show only the most useful candidates and say when more candidates exist.
End with discriminating follow-up questions derived from unresolved candidate differences.
follow_up_policy: Ask for additional identifier characters first when that would split the candidate set.
Ask for manufacturer, component/function, installation location, appearance, ATA, figure, or manual only when the missing field changes ranking.
Do not ask five generic questions merely to satisfy a benchmark count.
positive_examples: Query: I only know the part starts with 123 | Expected behavior: Search the 123 prefix, rank source-backed candidates, explain why 1234567 is only a candidate, and ask for the next characters or a differentiating clue.
Query: The part starts with 120-4 but I do not know the rest | Expected behavior: Use exact prefix search before semantic guidance and group candidates by source-resolved identity.
Query: I think the P/N contains 29073 | Expected behavior: Search contains fields and return 120-29073 variants with source strength and ambiguity.
Query: The component number contains 41824 but I do not know the prefix | Expected behavior: Search identifier contains indexes, not only page semantics.
Query: The P/N starts with MS49 and I cannot remember more | Expected behavior: Preserve the alphanumeric prefix and avoid normalizing away letters.
negative_examples: Query: Find part number 120-41824-003 | Expected behavior: This is exact identifier lookup, not partial discovery.
Query: Find a hinge in ATA 25-21-00 | Expected behavior: This is ATA plus description, not partial identifier discovery.
Query: Which page contains Figure 69? | Expected behavior: This is document/figure navigation.
known_failure_lessons: Q001 passed the old contract but produced generic candidate boilerplate; future output must explain why the candidate matches and what clue would distinguish it.
Do not let semantic page guidance outrank an exact prefix or contains match.
Do not ask broad generic follow-ups when candidate-level differences can produce a smaller, higher-information question set.

skill_cards.title: Exact identifier lookup
skill_cards.description: Resolve a complete part or item identifier using deterministic exact search before broader reasoning.
applies_when: The user supplies a complete part or item identifier.
The user asks where an exact identifier is listed or appears.
The user asks to locate or search for an exact P/N.
does_not_apply_when: The identifier is explicitly incomplete, a prefix, or a contains clue.
The apparent number is an ATA chapter rather than a part number.
skill_cards.reasoning_goal: Run deterministic exact identifier retrieval first, distinguish identity questions from location questions, and provide a direct source-backed answer when proof exists.
required_first_searches: Search exact normalized identifier fields without semantic expansion.
Resolve exact table/IPL and source page records.
Use page navigation when the user asks where the identifier appears.
forbidden_tunnels: Broad semantic retrieval before exact lookup.
Returning candidate boilerplate when exact proof exists.
Changing or fuzzy-correcting the supplied identifier without saying so.
ranking_policy: Exact character-for-character matches rank first.
Source-resolved table/IPL rows rank above OCR or semantic leads.
For location questions, rank the strongest indexed source page first and show supporting locations separately.
Do not merge distinct dash-number variants.

evidence_sufficiency.direct_answer_requires: An exact source-resolved identifier record or exact source page occurrence.
evidence_sufficiency.candidate_mode_when: Only non-source-resolved exact-looking guidance is available.
evidence_sufficiency.guidance_mode_when: Only OCR or semantic leads exist and exact source resolution fails.

answer_mode_rules.location_if: The user asks where, listed, appears, page, or manual location.
answer_mode_rules.candidate_if: The identifier appears only in guidance-level artifacts.

answer_requirements: Lead with the exact result or strongest indexed location.
Repeat the exact identifier exactly as supplied or explicitly state normalization.
Provide nomenclature, document, page, figure, or table context supported by current evidence.
Use candidate wording only when direct proof is absent.
Do not bury a successful exact match under process language.
follow_up_policy: Do not require follow-ups when the exact request is answered.
Ask for manual, aircraft, or variant only when exact duplicates remain unresolved.
For no-result cases, ask the user to verify characters or dash numbers.
positive_examples: Query: Find part number 120-41824-003 | Expected behavior: Search exact indexes first and return direct identity or exact source location.
Query: Where is P/N 120-41824-003 listed? | Expected behavior: Use document page navigation and show the strongest page plus supporting occurrences.
Query: Locate 120-48024-001 | Expected behavior: Preserve the full dash number and run exact lookup.
Query: Where does 120-48024-001 appear? | Expected behavior: Return page/document locations rather than a generic candidate list.
Query: Search for 120-34291-001 | Expected behavior: Use exact identifier search before semantic retrieval.
negative_examples: Query: The part starts with 120-4 | Expected behavior: This is partial identifier discovery.
Query: Locate a locking ring in manual 25-21-00 | Expected behavior: This is ATA plus description.
Query: Find a bracket part | Expected behavior: This is nomenclature discovery.
known_failure_lessons: Q073–Q080 found useful exact evidence but failed because executed tunnels were not represented in the plan; exact lookup must be a declared first search.
Do not answer a successful exact lookup with candidate-discovery boilerplate.
Location intent must change answer shape even when the underlying identifier is the same.

skill_cards.title: Nomenclature or function discovery
skill_cards.description: Find parts from a component name, physical role, or requested function while preserving the exact descriptive constraint.
applies_when: The user names a component such as hinge, bracket, latch, pin, or armrest.
The user describes what a component does rather than giving a part number.
The user asks for a part by nomenclature or installation function.
does_not_apply_when: A complete exact identifier is the main clue.
An ATA or manufacturer constraint should own the primary skill.
skill_cards.reasoning_goal: Preserve the requested noun or function, retrieve exact nomenclature and source-backed component evidence before broad semantics, and reject visually similar but semantically unrelated results.
required_first_searches: Search normalized nomenclature and table/IPL descriptions.
Search functional synonyms while retaining the original requested phrase.
Cross-link visual pages only after a relevant component identity is established.
forbidden_tunnels: Returning the same generic visual page for unrelated nouns.
Dropping the requested function during semantic expansion.
Treating visual similarity as nomenclature proof.
ranking_policy: Exact nomenclature matches outrank broad semantic similarity.
Functional matches must explain the relationship to the requested action.
Source-resolved table descriptions outrank visual guidance.
Penalize candidates that do not contain or clearly support the requested noun/function.

evidence_sufficiency.direct_answer_requires: A source-resolved component description matching the requested noun or function.
evidence_sufficiency.candidate_mode_when: Several plausible parts match the description or function.
evidence_sufficiency.guidance_mode_when: Only related pages or visual leads exist.

answer_mode_rules.direct_if: A source-resolved unique component clearly matches the request.
answer_mode_rules.guidance_if: Only related visual or semantic pages are available.

answer_requirements: Repeat the requested noun or function in the answer.
Explain how each candidate satisfies the description.
Separate exact nomenclature matches from functional inferences.
Do not present an unrelated visual page as the answer.
Ask for installation location, assembly, appearance, or manual only when it narrows candidates.
follow_up_policy: Ask which assembly or location contains the component when several matches remain.
Ask for appearance or nearby hardware for visually distinguishable candidates.
Ask for part-number characters, manufacturer, ATA, or manual only when relevant.
positive_examples: Query: Find me a bracket part | Expected behavior: Search exact BRACKET nomenclature and rank source-resolved candidates.
Query: I am looking for a latch | Expected behavior: Preserve LATCH and do not substitute unrelated covers or hinges.
Query: I need a part that lets the seat pivot | Expected behavior: Map pivot function to hinge/pivot components but label functional inference.
Query: Find the component that supports the armrest | Expected behavior: Retain armrest support as a two-part functional constraint.
Query: I need the item that retains the pin | Expected behavior: Search retain/pin descriptions and ask where the pin is installed if ambiguous.
negative_examples: Query: I need a Honeywell hinge part | Expected behavior: Manufacturer plus description should be primary.
Query: Find a hinge in ATA 25-21-00 | Expected behavior: ATA plus description should be primary.
Query: Find part number 120-41824-003 | Expected behavior: Exact identifier lookup.
known_failure_lessons: Several Q021–Q056 answers repeated the same visual pages for unrelated components; require noun/function relevance before ranking visual guidance.
Semantic similarity is guidance, not proof of nomenclature.
A safe answer can still be low quality when it ignores the requested component relationship.

skill_cards.title: ATA plus description discovery
skill_cards.description: Search within an ATA or manual-system constraint while preserving the requested component description.
applies_when: The user provides an ATA chapter and a component name or function.
The user names a manual chapter such as 25-21-00 and asks for a part.
The user uses an ATA constraint to narrow discovery.
does_not_apply_when: The number is clearly a complete part number rather than an ATA code.
skill_cards.reasoning_goal: Interpret the ATA value as a system/manual constraint, retain the component description, search inside that bounded area, and ask only for clues that distinguish remaining candidates.
required_first_searches: Resolve the ATA or manual-system scope.
Search source-resolved nomenclature/table records inside the ATA scope.
Use semantic or visual retrieval only as bounded guidance within the same scope.
forbidden_tunnels: Treating an ATA code as a part-number prefix.
Returning only a generic ATA description while ignoring the requested component.
Searching outside the ATA scope without an explicit repair reason.
ranking_policy: Candidates matching both ATA and component description rank first.
ATA-only pages without component relevance rank below source-resolved component records.
Exact nomenclature within the ATA scope outranks broad semantic similarity.
State when the ATA scope is known but no matching component is source-resolved.

evidence_sufficiency.direct_answer_requires: A source-resolved component record inside the requested ATA/manual scope.
evidence_sufficiency.candidate_mode_when: Multiple components inside the ATA scope match the description.
evidence_sufficiency.guidance_mode_when: Only ATA-level or semantic page leads exist.

answer_mode_rules.direct_if: One source-resolved component satisfies both ATA and description constraints.
answer_mode_rules.guidance_if: Only the ATA area is resolved, not the requested component.

answer_requirements: State that the number was interpreted as ATA/manual scope.
Repeat the requested component or function.
Show candidates that satisfy both constraints.
Do not stop after listing the ATA document area.
Use a candidate boundary when direct source evidence is absent.
follow_up_policy: Ask for part-number characters, manufacturer, installation location, figure, or manual page when those clues discriminate candidates.
Do not force a manufacturer question when it does not narrow the ATA candidate set.
Do not return zero follow-ups when the answer remains candidate-only and the benchmark expects guided discovery.
positive_examples: Query: Find a hinge in ATA 25-21-00 | Expected behavior: Scope to ATA 25-21-00 and search hinge nomenclature inside it.
Query: I need a seat bracket from ATA 25-21-00 | Expected behavior: Preserve both seat bracket and ATA constraints.
Query: Locate a locking ring in manual 25-21-00 | Expected behavior: Treat 25-21-00 as manual scope and search locking ring inside it.
Query: I want an armrest part in ATA 25 | Expected behavior: Search the broader ATA 25 scope while retaining armrest.
Query: Find a panel fastener under ATA 25 | Expected behavior: Require panel/fastener relevance inside ATA 25.
negative_examples: Query: The part starts with 25 | Expected behavior: Partial identifier unless ATA context is explicit.
Query: Find part number 120-41824-003 | Expected behavior: Exact identifier lookup.
Query: Find a hinge | Expected behavior: Nomenclature discovery without ATA.
known_failure_lessons: Q065–Q072 often resolved the ATA area but ignored the requested component and returned no follow-ups.
Correct ATA interpretation is not enough; the answer must also satisfy the descriptive constraint.
Candidate safety language and follow-up rendering must remain visible when no direct evidence exists.

skill_cards.title: Manufacturer plus description discovery
skill_cards.description: Search for a component while retaining an explicit manufacturer, vendor, or supplier constraint.
applies_when: The user names a manufacturer and a component.
The user requests a vendor-specific part family or function.
Manufacturer identity is a required narrowing constraint.
does_not_apply_when: A complete exact identifier is the stronger primary clue.
skill_cards.reasoning_goal: Retain manufacturer and component as separate mandatory constraints, distinguish confirmed manufacturer evidence from user-supplied preference, and avoid silently dropping the manufacturer during semantic retrieval.
required_first_searches: Resolve normalized manufacturer/vendor names and aliases.
Search source-resolved component descriptions with the manufacturer constraint.
Only broaden to component-only guidance when clearly labeled as not manufacturer-confirmed.
forbidden_tunnels: Dropping the manufacturer constraint without disclosure.
Claiming manufacturer identity from the user query alone.
Returning a generic component candidate as if it matched the named vendor.
ranking_policy: Source-resolved manufacturer plus component matches rank first.
Manufacturer-confirmed records outrank component-only candidates.
Component-only guidance may be shown separately but must not be labeled manufacturer-matched.
Vendor aliases may merge only when supported by reviewed normalization.

evidence_sufficiency.direct_answer_requires: Source evidence confirming both manufacturer and component identity.
evidence_sufficiency.candidate_mode_when: Manufacturer-scoped candidates exist but are not uniquely resolved.
evidence_sufficiency.guidance_mode_when: Only component matches or unverified vendor associations exist.

answer_mode_rules.direct_if: A source-resolved record confirms the named manufacturer and requested component.
answer_mode_rules.guidance_if: The component is found but manufacturer is not source-confirmed.

answer_requirements: Repeat the named manufacturer and requested component.
State whether manufacturer evidence is confirmed, missing, or only user-supplied.
Separate manufacturer-matched candidates from component-only leads.
Explain why each top candidate satisfies both constraints.
Do not imply vendor identity from document proximity.
follow_up_policy: Ask for part-number characters, vendor markings, manual, assembly, or installation location when useful.
Ask whether alternate or parent-company names are acceptable only when alias ambiguity exists.
Do not ask generic questions unrelated to manufacturer verification.
positive_examples: Query: I need a Honeywell hinge part | Expected behavior: Require source evidence for both Honeywell and hinge.
Query: Find an Embraer seat bracket | Expected behavior: Retain Embraer and seat bracket throughout ranking.
Query: I am looking for a Collins latch component | Expected behavior: Do not return a generic latch as Collins-confirmed.
Query: I want a Safran seat fitting | Expected behavior: Search Safran aliases and seat fitting descriptions.
Query: I am looking for a Parker valve component | Expected behavior: Require Parker evidence before making a vendor claim.
negative_examples: Query: Find me a bracket part | Expected behavior: No manufacturer constraint.
Query: Find a hinge in ATA 25-21-00 | Expected behavior: ATA plus description.
Query: Locate P/N 120-48024-001 | Expected behavior: Exact identifier lookup.
known_failure_lessons: Q057–Q064 often returned component matches without visible evidence that the named manufacturer was honored.
A user-supplied manufacturer is a search constraint, not proof that a candidate belongs to that manufacturer.
Component relevance cannot compensate for missing manufacturer verification.
